wave_title: Closes a correctness gap in the already-OBSERVED BUILD dependency census: a Cargo.lock dependency-array entry disambiguated as `"name version"` now resolves to its matching resolved package instead of being reported as an unresolved ambiguity. `.atlas/contracts/DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md`.

generation_model.G_n: eddb37d510 (docs(roadmap): correct stale R4.6-R4.12 status in donor-absorption plan) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: self-inspection of the dependency-census-cargo-bootstrap generation's own recorded scope: `adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs`'s `dependency_array_entry` explicitly discarded a lockfile entry's disambiguating version suffix, so any real same-crate-name/multiple-resolved-version situation would be reported as an unresolved ambiguity (a false closure-blocking negative) rather than correctly resolved -- a named, tested-as-absent, not-yet-exercised gap in the prior generation's own evidence record

priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity (priority 1 of the controller's own ordering) -- this is a latent bug in an already-materialized, already-OBSERVED capability (BUILD dependency census), not a new-capability extension, so it outranks further scope growth of the same feature (dependency closure, priority 6).

design_decisions.question: How much of Cargo.lock's disambiguation syntax to parse?
design_decisions.decision: Parse `"name"` and `"name version"`. The further `"name version (source)"` form (needed only when the same name AND version resolve from two distinct sources) is left as a named, documented, not-yet-materialized gap -- real Cargo.lock output for a pure-registry/workspace closure like this repository's own never needs it, and guessing at unparsed source-disambiguation input would violate the 'never claim a fact this extractor cannot prove' discipline.

design_decisions.question: What should happen when a disambiguated entry names a version with no matching [[package]] block?
design_decisions.decision: Report as a dangling reference with a distinct message ('no matching resolved version among N candidates'), not silently treated as unresolved ambiguity -- this is a different, more specific failure than genuine ambiguity and deserves a distinguishable diagnostic.

design_decisions.question: What should happen for a genuinely ambiguous entry (multiple candidates, no version suffix at all)?
design_decisions.decision: Still report as a dangling/ambiguous reference rather than guess. Real Cargo.lock output always disambiguates in this situation, so this path is adversarial/malformed-input coverage (a hand-edited or corrupted lockfile), not a live gap -- kept and tested per the falsification requirement, not deleted for being currently unreachable from real input.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: The fix correctly disambiguates a real same-name multi-version Cargo.lock entry, and does not regress this repository's own real (unambiguous) dependency closure.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: New unit tests in adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs: a positive disambiguation case (resolves to the correct version/checksum among two candidates), a named-version-with-no-match dangling case, and a no-version-suffix-with-multiple-candidates adversarial case.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: The existing, already-validated systemize CLI binary was run fresh against this repository's real root after the fix: dependency_closure.edges_total == 28, instances_total == 14, dangling_references == [] -- byte-identical to the pre-fix run, proving the fix introduces no regression against the one real corpus available (which has no live ambiguity to exercise the new code path on).
